config.title: Event Handling

intro.title: Event Handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive button that changes its displayed text when clicked. You will learn the core concept of event handling in React, which allows your application to respond to user actions like clicks. The main technologies involved are React's onClick event handler and TypeScript for type-safe function definitions. This will help you understand how to connect user interactions to updates in your component's state and UI.
intro.usecase: Event handling is the core mechanism behind every interactive UI in modern web applications. In real-world products, this pattern is used to capture user actions like submitting a form on a signup page, selecting filters on an e-commerce dashboard, or toggling a sidebar menu in a project management tool. As a developer, you'll implement event handlers to respond to clicks, input changes, and keyboard events, enabling dynamic features such as live search, modal popups, and real-time data validation. Mastering event handling allows you to build responsive interfaces that directly engage users, a fundamental skill for creating professional React applications.

objectives: Implement event handlers for common user interactions like clicks and input changes
Construct TypeScript interfaces to define event handler function signatures
Bind event handlers to React components using proper TypeScript typing
Manipulate component state in response to user events
Configure controlled form components with onChange event handlers
Integrate multiple event handlers within a single functional component
Update UI elements dynamically based on event-driven state changes

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing modules
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported React and useState correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named EventHandlingDemo that returns a div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should return a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the EventHandlingDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named EventHandlingDemo is defined and returns a div element.
successCriteria: The EventHandlingDemo component is defined and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your component is named EventHandlingDemo and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it EventHandlingDemo and it returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize state with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Inside your component, declare a state variable named 'count' using useState, initialize it to 0, and type it as number.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported. Provide the type annotation for the state variable as number.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [value, setValue] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a typed state variable 'count' initialized to 0.
successCriteria: A state variable 'count' is declared with useState, initialized to 0, and typed as number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've typed 'count' as number and initialized it to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state variable isn't properly typed or initialized. Review the useState syntax with TypeScript.

steps.title: Define an increment handler
steps.instruction: Inside the EventHandlingDemo component, create a function named handleIncrement that increments the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setCount with the updated value. You can use the current state to calculate the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component should have a handleIncrement function that updates the count state.
successCriteria: A function named handleIncrement is defined and calls setCount to increment the count state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named handleIncrement and properly updates the count state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it handleIncrement and it calls setCount to increment the count.

steps.title: Define a reset handler
steps.instruction: Inside your EventHandlingDemo component, define a function named handleReset that sets the count state back to 0.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount(0) to reset the count value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleReset function that resets the count state to 0 when called.
successCriteria: The handleReset function is defined and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a reset handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly resets the count to 0 using setCount(0).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleReset function is missing or doesn't reset the count to 0. Try creating a function that calls setCount(0).

steps.title: Add the count display
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value.
steps.hint: Use JSX syntax with curly braces to embed the count state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value in JSX

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element showing the current count value will appear in the component's output.
successCriteria: The paragraph element exists and displays the count state variable using curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the count state variable using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the count value correctly.

steps.title: Add the reset button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Add a second button with the text 'Reset' and wire its onClick event to the handleReset function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the existing increment button, using the same onClick syntax.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding another button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleReset}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have two buttons: 'Increment' and 'Reset', with the reset button wired to the reset handler.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Reset' is present and its onClick prop is set to handleReset.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Reset' and its onClick is set to handleReset.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is missing or not correctly wired. Add a <button> with onClick={handleReset} and text 'Reset'.

steps.title: Add an input field and change handler
steps.instruction: Define a handleChange function that updates the count state with the numeric value from an input field,
steps.hint: Create a function that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, extracts the value, converts it to a number, and calls setCount with that number. Then add an <input> element with onChange={handleChange}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleChange function that updates count based on input, and an input field wired to it.
successCriteria: A handleChange function is defined that takes a ChangeEvent, converts the input value to a number, and calls setCount. An <input> element with onChange={handleChange} is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined the handleChange function with the correct parameter type and added the input element with onChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the code: you need to define a handleChange function that updates count and add an input field with onChange.
